item.title: Refined proper descent for left completed sheaves on locally compact Hausdorff spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.25095v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We refine the proper descent of Postnikov completed sheaves on locally compact Hausdorff spaces to the dualizable world.
item.dc:creator: Li He

item.title: On simplicial maps with non-zero Hopf invariant
item.description: arXiv:2610.25562v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In general, it is interesting to investigate the complexity of simplicial maps under various topological constraints. In this paper, we consider maps between (triangulated oriented rational homology) manifolds with non-zero Hopf invariant and establish bounds on the simplicial complexity of the fiber of a regular point. The lower bound, which is cubic in the dimension, is proved via a refinement of a theorem of S. Eilenberg. The upper bound is notable in that it is uniform with respect to the Hopf invariant.
item.dc:creator: Sergei Vad. Fomin

item.title: A New Proof of Wei's Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.25838v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the paper \emph{Structure and realizability for rational maps}, Wei proved the following. Let \(k\) nontrivial partitions of an integer \(d\ge 3\) be given, satisfying the Riemann--Hurwitz formula for the case of maps between two spheres. If \(k>\ell+1\), where \[ \ell=\min_i|\pi_i| \] is the shortest partition length, then there exists a rational map whose branch datum is given by these partitions. In this paper we give a new proof of Wei's theorem on realizing a tuple of partitions as the ramification data of a rational function. The proof is inductive on the shortest partition length. Two auxiliary results are established: a two-cut partition theorem and a gluing theorem for marked spherical coverings. These reduce any counterexample with shortest length \(\ell\ge3\) to auxiliary data with either fewer factors or smaller shortest length, while preserving the total defect and the marked conditions. The base case \(\ell\le2\) is quoted from the literature.
item.dc:creator: Zhiqaing Wei, Mengyan Xing, Xingya Zhao

item.title: Adelic Asphericity and One-Relator Pro-\(p\) Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.26288v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a direct Fox-calculus proof of the known rational asphericity theorem for every finite presentation complex with one nontrivial relator, including proper powers. The proof uses completed Fox derivatives and the absence of zero divisors in the completed algebra of a prounipotent group. Exact scalar extension to the finite adeles then yields adelic asphericity and a product decomposition of the higher homotopy groups of integral Bousfield--Kan completion. We also prove rational and pro-\(p\) analogues of Mannan's formula for finite two-complexes, with their natural topologies and fundamental group actions. The rational cohomological Whitehead criterion is proved directly. For a discrete one-relator group with relator not a proper power, we show that the tower \(L_2\nu_n(G)\) is Mittag--Leffler. Consequently \(\limone_nL_2\nu_n(G)=0\), and \(\pi_2(\Z_\infty BG)\) is naturally the inverse limit of the nilpotent Baer invariants. We identify this Baer limit canonically and topologically with the kernel of the integral augmentation-completed Fox operator and with the product of its local pro-\(p\) kernels. The comparison yields a torsion-free profinite homotopy module, vanishing inverse limits of the finite-stage transgression kernels, and explicit lifting obstructions. These results provide a homotopy-theoretic framework for the question of Serre in Gildenhuys's corrected formulation.
item.dc:creator: Andrey Mikhovich

item.title: On the notion of $\mathbb{A}^1$-coverings
item.description: arXiv:2610.26345v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the notion of $\mathbb{A}^1$-$n$-coverings and begin the development of their theory over an arbitrary base scheme $S$, in analogy to that of higher coverings in an $\infty$-topos. We show that for $n=0$, our notion recovers Morel's $\mathbb{A}^1$-coverings between simplicial sheaves. Under suitable assumptions, we then provide a Galois-theoretic classification of $\mathbb{A}^1$-$n$-coverings. Finally, we answer a question of Morel concerning a geometric criterion for $\mathbb{A}^1$-coverings in the negative.
item.dc:creator: Marco Giustetto, Thor Wittich

item.title: $\mathbb{C}$-Motivic Eilenberg-Mac Lane Spectra as $\mathrm{MGL}$-Motivic Thom Spectra and Normed $\mathbb{G}_m$-Hochschild Homology
item.description: arXiv:2610.26771v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We exhibit the $p$-complete $\mathbb{C}$-motivic Eilenberg-Mac Lane spectra $\mathrm{M}\mathbb{F}_p$ and $(\mathrm{M}\mathbb{Z})_p^{\wedge}$ as $\mathbb{E_3}$-$\mathrm{MGL}_p^{\wedge}$-motivic Thom spectra over the motivic $\mathbb{G}_m$-loop spaces $\Omega_{\mathbb{G}_m}\mathrm{BGL}$ and $\Omega_{\mathbb{G}_m}\mathrm{BSL}$, respectively. Furthermore, for $p=2$, we compute the $\mathrm{MGL}_2^{\wedge}$-relative $\mathbb{G}_m$-Hochschild Homology $\mathbb{G}_m \odot^{\mathrm{MGL}_2^{\wedge}} {-}$, recently introduced by Bachmann-Burklund-Dundas-{\O}stv{\ae}r, of $\mathrm{M}\mathbb{F}_2$ and $(\mathrm{M}\mathbb{Z})_2^{\wedge}$ to be $\mathrm{M}\mathbb{F}_2[\mathrm{BGL}]$ and $(\mathrm{M}\mathbb{Z})_2^{\wedge}[\mathrm{BSL}]$ as $\mathbb{E}_2$-$\mathrm{M}\mathbb{F}_2$-algebras and $\mathbb{E}_2$-$(\mathrm{M}\mathbb{Z})_2^{\wedge}$-algebras, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Preston Cranford

item.title: An Atiyah-Segal homomorphism for approximate representations of infinite groups, and almost multiplicative ucp maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.24252v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Atiyah-Segal homomorphism relates the representation ring of a finite group to the $K$-theory ring of its classifying space. We develop a version of this for infinite groups, but based on a ring of approximate representations rather than representations. We then use known results on the Baum-Connes conjecture to show that our homomorphism is an isomorphism for many groups: this includes all torsion-free amenable groups, and all torsion-free fundamental groups of compact manifolds of dimension at most three. The main motivation is the desire to understand approximate representations using topological tools: as a sample application we give some examples of torsion phenomena in approximate representation theory. The methods of proof are $C^*$-algebraic: the key idea is to relate our Atiyah-Segal type homomorphism to Kasparov's coassembly map. The main step realizes (Hausdorffized) $KK$-theory as approximately multiplicative ucp maps modulo stable approximate unitary equivalence for appropriate $C^*$-algebras. This is in the spirit of the stable uniqueness theorems of Dadarlat-Eilers and Lin, and may be of purely $C^*$-algebraic interest.
item.dc:creator: Rufus Willett

item.title: Cospan contexts and higher categories
item.description: arXiv:2610.24473v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Motivated by the desire to turn the cobordism hypothesis (a statement about the universal property of some $n$-category of bordisms) into a $1$-categorical statement, we prove that all $n$-categories can be modeled by \emph{$n$-cospan contexts}: these are $1$-categories equipped with a collection of iterated cospans that satisfy a composition property in terms of pushouts. In particular, we construct an adjunction from $\mathsf{Cat}_n$ to the category of $n$-cospan contexts which simultaneously generalizes the $n$-fold span construction of Haugseng and the twisted arrow category construction (when $n = 1$).
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Riva

item.title: A characterization of finite modular 2-groups via magnitude homology
item.description: arXiv:2610.25030v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Finite quasihamiltonian groups - that is, finite groups in which every pair of subgroups commutes - admit several characterizations. In this work, after introducing the notion of sectional contractibility graph, we provide a new characterization in terms of (a suitable subgroup of) magnitude homology. Our approach especially focuses on the subgroup lattices of finite groups and on the related notion of modularity. We present a detailed study for finite 2-groups, and, in particular, in the case of extraspecial 2-groups and Pauli groups. These groups, of interest because of their diverse applications in both mathematics and physics, already describe the wealth of information that one can obtain in restricting the study to the case of 2-groups.
item.dc:creator: Luigi Caputi, Francesco G. Russo

item.title: The minimum number of vertices of a triangulation of $\mathbb{RP}^5$
item.description: arXiv:2610.25171v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a computer-assisted proof that every finite simplicial triangulation of real projective five-space has at least twenty-four vertices. Together with the construction of Guyer, Steinerberger, and Yang, this determines the minimum. A cup-product argument produces an induced subcomplex on sixteen or seventeen vertices. Transfer to the spherical double cover then imposes a covering condition on its lifted faces. In the sixteen-vertex case, a direct capacity bound excludes twenty-two vertices. For twenty-three vertices, a cochain extension argument reduces every relevant completion to one of 115 critical signed complexes; integer weights and exact covering certificates exclude all of them. The argument requires no assumption that the triangulation is combinatorial.
item.dc:creator: Xinrui Chang (Fudan University)

item.title: Finitely enhanced nontopological triangulated categories
item.description: arXiv:2610.25198v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Over every nonzero commutative ring $R$, we construct a nontopological triangulated category over $R$, whose finitely generated thick subcategories are alegbraic, while the scalar action of $R$ is faithful.
item.dc:creator: Chencheng Zhang

item.title: Negative-Definite Plumbings and New Unknotting Numbers
item.description: arXiv:2610.25430v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We use Neumann's normal form to decide whether the double branched cover of a knot bounds a negative-definite plumbing tree in either orientation, starting from the recognised Seifert or graph-manifold structure of the cover. For many non-alternating knots with at most thirteen crossings whose unknotting numbers were unknown, this identifies the cases in which the Heegaard Floer homology of the cover can be computed from such a plumbing, and shows for most of the others that it cannot. We determine 112 new unknotting numbers. For 43 of them, the lower bound rests on Heegaard Floer homology computed from the plumbing; for the other 69, it comes from linking pairings and from a theorem of McCoy and Park on special alternating knots. Finally, we show that the knot 13n1587 is a further explicit counterexample to the Bernhard--Jablan conjecture, after 13n3370.
item.dc:creator: Seong-Jin Lee

item.title: Homotopy distributions for Vietoris-Rips complexes of random circle samples
item.description: arXiv:2610.26366v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the distribution of the homotopy type of the Vietoris-Rips complex of a fixed number of independent uniform points on a circle. An exact identity expresses each binomial moment of a periodic-orbit count as one probability for circular gaps, multiplied by a constant avoidance factor. We evaluate these probabilities by finite lattice-point counts and interpolation, obtaining explicit formulas for every sample size and every real scale. On an explicit rational partition, the probabilities are continuous piecewise polynomials of degree at most one less than the sample size. We also determine the homotopy distribution in the first transition window above each positive critical fraction $c_t=t/(2t+1)$. In this window the number of critical periodic orbits converges to a Poisson law with explicit intensity, yielding the limiting probabilities of the preceding odd sphere, the contractible type, and every wedge multiplicity of the critical even sphere.
item.dc:creator: Jaemin Park (Department of Mathematics,Research Institute of Natural Sciences, Sookmyung Women's University)

item.title: On The Acyclic MacPhersonian
item.description: arXiv:1504.06592v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The acyclic MacPhersonian $\AM_n^d$ is the poset of acyclic oriented matroids of rank $d+1$ on $n$ labelled elements, the combinatorial model of the space of configurations of $n$ points spanning $\R^d$ up to affine equivalence, which is the Grassmannian $G(d,n-1)$. We study it inside the larger poset $\Sep_n^d$ of \emph{spherical separoids}, those acyclic separoids whose Radon complex is a sphere of the dimension of the space of affine dependences. Our main unconditional results are as follows. Over every poset of spherical separoids that contains the realizable oriented matroids there is a tautological sphere fibration, and its Stiefel--Whitney classes show that the mod~$2$ cohomology ring of $G(d,n-1)$ is a ring retract of that of the poset, for all $n$ and $d$. For $d=n-2$ the poset of spherical separoids is homotopy equivalent to $G(n-2,n-1)$, and contains $\AM_n^{n-2}$ as a homotopy equivalent subposet. A fat model of $\AM_n^d$ made of piecewise geodesic antipodal spheres in the round sphere is weakly homotopy equivalent to its order complex. The chirotope of every such sphere is recovered from the degrees of its coordinate projections. We then analyse a strategy based on the mean curvature flow. Any argument that follows the combinatorial type of a sphere generically along the flow would connect every uniform oriented matroid to a realizable one by mutations. By a theorem of Gu and Knauer this is impossible in every rank $r\ge7$ on $n\ge r+17$ elements, so the flow must leave the oriented matroids. We show that the basin hypothesis of the flow, together with the property that $\|\AM_n^d\|$ is a homology manifold, implies $\|\AM_n^d\|\simeq G(d,n-1)$, without following types along the flow. We conclude with the open problems and conjectures that remain.
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Strausz

item.title: Units of $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$-equivariant $K$-theory and bundles of UHF-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2410.06947v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider infinite tensor product actions of a finite cyclic group $G$ on the UHF-algebra $D = \text{End}(V)^{\otimes \infty}$ for a finite-dimensional projectively faithful unitary $G$-representation $V$ and determine the equivariant homotopy type of the group $\text{Aut}(D \otimes \mathbb{K})$, where $\mathbb{K}$ are the compact operators on $\ell^2(G) \otimes H_0$ for a separable Hilbert space $H_0$ with $\dim(H_0) = \infty$. We show that this group carries an equivariant infinite loop space structure revealing it as the first space of a naive $G$-spectrum. We identify this spectrum with the positive units $gl_1(KU^D)_+$ of equivariant $KU^D$-theory, which was not possible in the case of circle actions considered by Evans and the second author. Here, $KU^D$ is a $G$-spectrum representing $X \mapsto K_*^G(C(X) \otimes D)$. As a consequence the first group of the cohomology theory associated to $gl_1(KU^D)_+$ classifies equivariant $D \otimes \mathbb{K}$-bundles over finite $G$-CW-complexes.
item.dc:creator: Valerio Bianchi, Ulrich Pennig

item.title: Integral cohomology of classical Artin groups: spherical types $A,C,D$ and affine types $\widetilde B,\widetilde C,\widetilde D$
item.description: arXiv:2609.15419v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We determine the additive structure of the integral cohomology groups with trivial coefficients of the Artin groups in the spherical families $A_n,C_n,D_n$ and the affine families $\widetilde B_n,\widetilde C_n,\widetilde D_n$. We first compute the integral cohomology of braid groups by algebraic methods and then use the Salvetti complexes to express the cohomology of the remaining families in terms of these computations. The resulting descriptions apply in every admissible rank. For each family, we establish cohomological stabilization and show that the integral cohomology groups contain no elements of order $p^2$ for any prime $p$. We also give uniform generating series formulas describing the stable integral cohomology in terms of that of the braid groups.
item.dc:creator: F. V. Weinstein

item.title: Equivariant bordism rigidity for toric manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2609.27412v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we develop a bordism-theoretic approach to rigidity problems for toric and quasitoric manifolds. We prove that two toric manifolds are isomorphic as varieties if and only if they are weakly equivariantly unitary bordant. We also establish a parallel rigidity result for omnioriented quasitoric manifolds satisfying the injectivity condition, showing that their equivariant unitary bordism classes completely determine their omniorientation-preserving equivariant homeomorphism types. Thus, equivariant bordism provides a topological framework for detecting geometric and combinatorial rigidity.
item.dc:creator: Runze Chen, Yuanxin Guan, Zhi L\"{u}

item.title: LandscapeSHAP: Which Persistent Homology Class Gets the Credit?
item.description: arXiv:2609.31469v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Shapley values, a solution concept from cooperative game theory, have recently become a standard tool for feature credit allocation in machine learning. They provide an axiomatically justified method to fairly distribute a model's prediction among the data features. Shapley values have not yet been applied to explain machine learning models trained on features from topological data analysis. We develop what we believe is the first such approach, focusing on the persistence landscape featurization of persistence diagrams. Because each landscape coordinate is a rank statistic, crediting a model's prediction back to individual persistent homology classes (persistence diagram points) is nontrivial. We introduce LandscapeSHAP, a method for fair credit allocation to persistence diagram points based on a model's prediction. For linear models on persistence landscapes, LandscapeSHAP has a closed form expression that gives the exact Shapley value of every persistence diagram point. In particular, there is no coalition sampling required. We further prove that the four Shapley "fairness" axioms uniquely characterize this credit allocation for any model, not only linear ones. For a general nonlinear model, this unique value can only be calculated exactly from its defining coalition averaging formula, which requires considering all $2^N$ many coalitions, where $N$ is the number of points in the persistence diagram. This is computationally intractable for persistence diagrams of realistic size. We complement the exact linear model result with an efficient Monte Carlo sampling of persistence diagram coalitions. We give convergence rates in terms of number of samples needed to approximate to a desired degree of accuracy. We also prove stability results for the LandscapeSHAP credit allocation, for any model.
item.dc:creator: Nikola Mili\'cevi\'c

item.title: BV rigidity for compact Lie groups and the integral string topology of the symplectic group
item.description: arXiv:2610.04164v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $G$ be a connected compact Lie group and $R$ a commutative ring over which $H_*(G;R)$ is an exterior algebra on odd primitive generators. We prove a rigidity theorem: the Batalin-Vilkovisky (BV) algebra $\mathbb{H}_*(LG;R)$ of Chas and Sullivan on the homology of the free loop space is that of the product of odd spheres with the classical exponents of $G$, tensored with the group ring of the torsion of $\pi_1(G)$. Conversely, over an integral domain the graded algebra $\mathbb{H}_*(LG;R)$ already determines the exponents and the group ring, hence the BV algebra. If moreover $G$ is simply connected, then $\mathbb{H}_*(LG;R)$, as a BV algebra, is the Hochschild cohomology of $H^*(G;R)$ with the BV operator induced by Poincar\'e duality. The isomorphism with the product of spheres is algebraic: for $\mathrm{Sp}(n)$, $n\geq2$, and $\mathrm{SU}(n)$, $n\geq3$, no map of spaces induces it over $\mathbb{Z}$. We compute, in Hepworth's presentation, the integral BV algebra $\mathbb{H}_*(L\mathrm{Sp}(n);\mathbb{Z})$ with its Gerstenhaber bracket, open for $n\geq2$, the running example of the rigidity theorem.
item.dc:creator: Mukilraj K (Indian Institute of Science Education,Research Kolkata, India)

item.title: Nullhomotopic equivariant shifts and Borsuk-Ulam-compatible compact abelian groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.10111v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We disprove the classical version of the Borsuk-Ulam-flavored conjecture, due to Baum-D{\k{a}}browski-Hajac, that free actions $X\times \mathbb{G}\to X$ on non-empty compact Hausdorff spaces by non-trivial compact groups admit no equivariant maps $X*\mathbb{G}\to X$. Specifically, among non-trivial compact abelian $\mathbb{G}$, the conjecture fails precisely when $\mathbb{G}$ is torsion-free profinite.
item.dc:creator: Alexandru Chirvasitu, Alexander D\k{a}browski

item.title: James reduced product schemes and double quasisymmetric functions
item.description: arXiv:2304.11508v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Symmetric function theory is a key ingredient in the Schubert calculus of Grassmannians. Quasisymmetric functions are analogues that are similarly central to algebraic combinatorics, but for which the associated geometry is poorly developed. Baker and Richter (2008) showed that $\operatorname{QSym}$ manifests topologically as the cohomology ring of the loop suspension of infinite projective space or equivalently of its combinatorial homotopy model, the James reduced product $J\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^\infty$. In recent work, we used this viewpoint to develop topologically-motivated bases of $\operatorname{QSym}$ and initiate a Schubert calculus for $J\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^\infty$ in both cohomology and $K$-theory. Here, we study the torus-equivariant cohomology of $J\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^\infty$. We identify a cellular basis and introduce double monomial quasisymmetric functions as combinatorial representatives, analogous to the factorial Schur functions and double Schubert polynomials of classical Schubert calculus. We also provide a combinatorial Littlewood--Richardson-type rule for the structure coefficients of this basis. Furthermore, we introduce an algebro-geometric analogue of the James reduced product construction. In particular, we prove that the James reduced product of a complex (quasi-)projective variety also carries the structure of a (quasi-)projective variety.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Pechenik, Matthew Satriano

item.title: Splitting vector bundles over real algebraic varieties
item.description: arXiv:2511.15616v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Suppose $X$ is a smooth affine real variety and $\mathscr{E}$ is a vector bundle over $X$. We analyze the problem of splitting off a free rank one summand from $\mathscr{E}$ in corank $0$ and $1$. The problem in corank $0$ can be viewed as the search for a real analog of Murthy's celebrating splitting theorem in the algebraically closed case: to wit, beyond the vanishing of the top Chern class in Chow theory, are the obstructions to splitting ``purely topological''? In a sense, the answer in this case is yes, and we give a proof, using motivic techniques, of a mild extension of the results of Bhatwadekar-Sridharan and Bhatwadekar-Das-Mandal. In corank $1$, in the algebraically closed situation, Murthy's splitting conjecture (now a theorem in characteristic $0$) predicts that the vanishing of the top Chern class in Chow theory is the only obstruction to splitting off a free rank $1$ summand, and we can search for a suitable ``real'' analog of this assertion. We observe that several natural guesses for a ``real'' analog of Murthy's splitting conjecture cannot be true, i.e., that the situation over the real numbers is rather complicated.
item.dc:creator: Aravind Asok, Jean Fasel, Samuel Lerbet

item.title: Computing the Hopf invariant
item.description: arXiv:2512.03201v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider Whitehead's integral formula and propose an algorithm for computing the Hopf invariant for simplicial mappings.
item.dc:creator: Oleg R. Musin, Timur Shamazov

item.title: Computations on the tautological basis of the cohomology ring of the Peterson variety
item.description: arXiv:2602.14605v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: It is known that the set of square free monomials on the Chern classes of the tautological line bundles over the Peterson variety forms an additive basis of its cohomology ring. We study the expansion formula for their products. In particular, we give a square free expansion of the products multiplying degree 2 classes in terms of elementary symmetric polynomials and binomial coefficients.
item.dc:creator: Yuito Hashimoto

item.title: PTOPOFL: Topology-Guided Personalised Federated Learning with Persistent-Homology Client Descriptors
item.description: arXiv:2603.04323v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Clustered and personalised federated learning (FL) needs a signal telling the server which clients should share a model. Most methods derive it from losses or model updates that must be recomputed during training. We study pTopoFL, which derives it once, before training, from a compact persistent-homology (PH) descriptor of each client's feature distribution: the server clusters clients on these descriptors, weights them within clusters, and runs blended clustered local gradient descent, returning one personalised model per cluster. For strongly convex, smooth losses we analyse the complete procedure: for any partition, one round is a contraction with factor (1-eta*mu)^tau; the fixed point is characterised by a local-step drift bound, an exact formula for the effective strength of blending (which yields a calibration rule) and a stochastic floor exposing a bias-variance trade-off of clustering; and personalisation lowers the heterogeneity floor in proportion to a measurable share of the dispersion of client optima. Experiments on synthetic federations, a label-skew benchmark and a real four-hospital dataset confirm the theory and delimit the method. When feature geometry and decision rules co-vary, the PH partition recovers the latent client groups, including differences a linear-subspace descriptor misses, and pTopoFL is competitive with the strongest clustered baselines; on the real federation it lowers the test log-loss of FedAvg from 0.463 to 0.438, on par with the best personalised methods. When heterogeneity is invisible in feature geometry, it offers no advantage over FedAvg. pTopoFL transmits model parameters and is no more private than FedAvg; we give a record-level differential-privacy accounting and show that privatising the descriptor destroys the partition. Code reproduces every number.
item.dc:creator: Kelly L Vomo-Donfack, Adryel Hoszu, Gr\'egory Ginot, Ian Morilla

item.title: Quotient Geometry and Persistence-Stable Metrics for Swarm Configurations
item.description: arXiv:2603.18041v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Can temporal information recover geometry lost by a persistence diagram? For $n\ge3$ points on the unit sphere evolving under known homogeneous complete consensus, we prove generic local recovery modulo rotations and permutations from two ordinary zero-dimensional Vietoris--Rips persistence snapshots. The structural result applies to every labeled tree: its edge inner products and their first temporal derivatives have differential rank $2n-3$, exactly the dimension of the regular formation quotient. An explicit pole--equator witness proves this simultaneously for all tree types after taking a finite intersection of open dense sets. Although one snapshot has generic local fibers of dimension $n-2$, two sufficiently close snapshots are injective on a common neighborhood. The optimal inverse Lipschitz constant grows as $\Theta(1/|h|)$ when the sampling interval tends to zero. A verified left inverse, interval derivative bounds, and explicit persistence-matching margins certify neighborhoods and time intervals at rational reference formations. The results are local and model-specific; reflection ambiguity and centered rank obstructions remain.
item.dc:creator: Mark M. Bailey

item.title: \'Etale Fundamental Groups: a geometric and topological approach to fundamental groups in algebraic geometry
item.description: arXiv:2606.23906v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This thesis explores the notion of fundamental groups across three mathematical settings. We begin with the classical topological theory of covering spaces, highlighting its structural analogy with Galois theory. We then follow Grothendieck in transporting these ideas to algebraic geometry. The inadequacy of the Zariski topology motivates the \'etale topology, from which the \'etale fundamental group is constructed and compared to its topological counterpart via transcendental methods. Finally, we linearise the theory through Tannakian duality, where fundamental groups are recovered as automorphism groups of fibre functors on certain monoidal categories, a framework broad enough to encompass \'etale, topological, and motivic Galois groups alike.
item.dc:creator: Loris De Vos

item.title: Cellular $\mathbb{A}^1$-homology of wonderful models of subspace arrangements
item.description: arXiv:2607.29097v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We compute the cellular $\mathbb{A}^1$-homology of De Concini--Procesi wonderful models of subspace arrangements. For a building set $\mathcal{G}$ over a field $k$, we identify the cellular $\mathbb{A}^1$-chain complex of $\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{G})$ with an $\eta$-twisted nested-set complex carrying Milnor--Witt coefficients and derived orientation data. The key geometric input is a motivic blow-up calculation: for a blow-up along a smooth center of codimension $c$, the relevant connecting class is $(c-1)_\epsilon\eta$, hence it is zero for $c$ odd and $\eta$ for $c$ even. This replaces the parity condition in the computation of Rains by a Milnor--Witt attaching class. As a consequence, the part of cellular $\mathbb{A}^1$-homology surviving after multiplication by $\eta$, and also the homology after inverting $\eta$, are expressed by the interval cohomology of the $2$-divisible subposet of the lattice generated by $\mathcal{G}$. For the braid arrangement, the condition becomes the odd-block condition on partitions, yielding explicit decompositions for the cellular $\mathbb{A}^1$-homology of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{0,N}$ and examples in low rank.
item.dc:creator: Haoyang Liu, Keyao Peng
